quote: Building autonomous information seeking agency involves addressing a set of challenges that span web environment perception and decision-making: (1) acquiring high-quality, fine-grained browsing data that reflects diverse user intents and rich interaction contexts, (2) constructing reliable trajectories that support long-horizon reasoning and task decomposition, and (3) designing scalable and generalizable training strategies.
claim: WebDancer identifies three key challenges in building autonomous information-seeking agents: data quality, trajectory construction, and scalable training.

quote: We synthesise the datasets in two ways: 1). By crawling web pages to construct deep queries, referred to as crawlQA, enabling the acquisition of web information through click actions. 2). By enhancing easy-to-hard QA pairs synthesis to incentivize the progression from weak-to-strong agency, transforming simple questions into complex ones, termed e2hQA.
claim: WebDancer proposes two dataset synthesis methods: crawlQA from web crawling and e2hQA for easy-to-hard question transformation.

quote: To enable more efficient and effective training, we adopt a two-stage approach combining rejection sampling fine-tuning (RFT) with subsequent on-policy RL. For the trajectory sampling, we restrict the action space to two commonly effective web information-seeking tools as action: search and click.
claim: WebDancer uses a two-stage training pipeline: RFT followed by on-policy RL with search and click actions.

quote: Building on the SFT stage, RL employs Decoupled Clip and Dynamic Sampling Policy Optimization algorithm to refine and incentivize the policy model's ability to interleave Thought-Action-Observation sequences.
claim: WebDancer employs the DAPO algorithm for RL training to optimize thought-action-observation interleaving.

quote: Among Open-sourced frameworks, agentic approaches built on top of native strong reasoning models like QwQ-32B consistently outperform their non-agentic counterparts, demonstrating the effectiveness of leveraging reasoning-specialized models in agent construction.
claim: WebDancer shows that reasoning-specialized models (QwQ-32B) outperform non-agentic baselines on GAIA and WebWalkerQA.

quote: By introducing scalable QA data synthesis methods and a two-stage training pipeline combining SFT and on-policy RL, our WebDancer agent achieves strong performance on GAIA and WebWalkerQA.
claim: WebDancer's key contribution is a systematic framework combining data synthesis and two-stage training for web agents.

quote: Currently, we integrate only two basic information-seeking tools. To enable more advanced and fine-grained retrieval capabilities, we plan to incorporate more sophisticated tools, such as browser modeling by abstracting browser functionalities into modular tools, and a Python sandbox environment.
claim: WebDancer is limited to only two tools (search and click) and plans to add browser modeling and Python sandbox.

quote: While we have accumulated a large corpus of QA pairs and corresponding trajectories, effectively scaling learning remains a challenge, particularly in the RL stage, where only a small subset (e.g., 5,000 pairs) can be utilized due to computational and stability constraints of RL in agentic tasks.
claim: WebDancer faces RL scalability limitations, using only 5,000 QA pairs due to computational constraints.

quote: In this work, we introduce IterResearch, an Iterative Deep-Research Paradigm that reformulates deep research as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). Unlike the mono-contextual approach that suffers from unbounded state expansion and noise contamination, IterResearch periodically consolidates its findings into a synthesized report and reconstructs its workspace.
claim: WebResearcher proposes IterResearch, which reformulates deep research as an MDP with periodic state reconstruction.

quote: At each round i, the agent's state s_i consists of three components: (1) The original research Question q, (2) The evolving Reporti-1 from the previous round (empty for i=1), and (3) The most recent Actioni-1 and its Tool Responsei-1 (if i>1).
claim: IterResearch maintains a compact state with question, evolving report, and latest action-observation tuple.

section: 3 A Scalable Data Engine for Advancing Agentic Intelligence
quote: Our engine leverages a collaborative multi-agent framework organized into a three-stage iterative workflow: (1) seed data generation, (2) iterative complexity escalation, and (3) rigorous quality control.
claim: WebFrontier data engine uses three stages: seed generation, complexity escalation, and quality control.

section: 4.3 Research-Synthesis: Harnessing Test-time Scaling with IterResearch
quote: The framework consists of two distinct phases: Parallel Research and Integrative Synthesis. The former phase fosters the concurrent exploration of diverse problem-solving approaches, while the latter integrates these disparate perspectives into a single, unified solution.
claim: Research-Synthesis Framework enables test-time scaling through parallel research and integrative synthesis phases.

section: General Web Navigation and Reasoning Benchmarks.
quote: On Humanity's Last Exam (HLE), arguably one of the most challenging benchmarks for frontier AI systems, WebResearcher-heavy achieves 36.7% accuracy—dramatically outperforming all systems including DeepSeek-V3.1 (29.8%), OpenAI Deep Research (26.6%), and Gemini Deep Research (26.9%).
claim: WebResearcher achieves 36.7% on HLE, outperforming DeepSeek-V3.1 (29.8%) and proprietary systems.

quote: On GAIA, WebResearcher achieves 72.8% accuracy, surpassing all evaluated systems including Claude-4-Sonnet (68.3%) and OpenAI-o3 (70.5%), with a remarkable 9.7 percentage point improvement over DeepSeek-V3.1 (63.1%).
claim: WebResearcher achieves 72.8% on GAIA, surpassing all evaluated systems including Claude-4-Sonnet and OpenAI-o3.

quote: This study introduces BrowseComp-ZH, the first benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the web browsing and reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) in the Chinese information environment.
claim: BrowseComp-ZH is the first Chinese-language web browsing benchmark for LLMs

quote: We construct 289 high-quality samples across 11 diverse topics, including Film & TV, History, Technology, Medicine, and more.
claim: BrowseComp-ZH contains 289 questions across 11 domains

quote: To ensure the high difficulty of each question and the uniqueness of each answer, we implement a rigorous two-stage quality control pipeline that includes a three-engine keyword validation process and human-in-the-loop verification.
claim: BrowseComp-ZH uses two-stage quality control with keyword retrievability and answer uniqueness validation

quote: Most standalone LLMs—such as GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-72B, and Llama-4—achieve limited accuracy, highlighting the difficulty of the benchmark.
claim: Naive LLMs perform poorly on BrowseComp-ZH with accuracy below 10%

quote: AI search products employing multi-turn retrieval, including DeepResearch (42.9%) and Doubao (Deep Search) (26.0%), further outperform purely parametric models.
claim: Agentic systems with multi-turn retrieval achieve up to 42.9% accuracy on BrowseComp-ZH

quote: This work presents a paradigm-shifting framework for synthesizing training data WebShaper for information-seeking (IS) agents through formalization-driven design.
claim: WebShaper introduces formalization-driven data synthesis for information-seeking agents

quote: By establishing a set theory-based mathematical formalization of IS tasks, we address critical limitations in existing information-driven approaches that suffer from structural inconsistencies, task controllability, diversity, and coverage.
claim: WebShaper uses set theory-based Knowledge Projections (KP) to formalize information-seeking tasks

quote: To mitigate these limitations, we introduce the Layer-wise Expansion Strategy. We layer-wisely traverse the graph to find all leaf constants.
claim: WebShaper uses Layer-wise Expansion Strategy to avoid redundancy and reasoning shortcuts

quote: Experimental results demonstrate that WebShaper not only achieves state-of-the-art performance on GAIA and WebWalkerQA benchmarks but also introduces controllability over task design.
claim: WebShaper achieves SOTA performance on GAIA and WebWalkerQA benchmarks

quote: The composition of proposed Knowledge Projections enables precise engineering of reasoning structures and complexity.
claim: Knowledge Projections enable precise engineering of reasoning structures and complexity

quote: We introduce WebWalkerQA, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs' web traversal abilities in complex, multi-step information-seeking tasks.
claim: WebWalkerQA is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs' web traversal abilities

quote: Experiments show that WebWalkerQA effectively challenges RAG systems, and combining RAG with WebWalker improves web navigation performance.
claim: WebWalkerQA challenges RAG systems; combining RAG with WebWalker improves performance

quote: Through such data construction method with LLM and human participation, we obtain 680 question-answer pairs for WebWalkerQA.
claim: WebWalkerQA contains 680 question-answer pairs across 4 domains

quote: The proportions of the conference, organization, education, and game domains are 24.0%, 7.9%, 46.3%, and 24.0%, respectively. In terms of language distribution, Chinese and English account for 60.5%, 39.5%, respectively.
claim: WebWalkerQA is bilingual with 60.5% Chinese and 39.5% English

quote: Single-source QAs are labeled as {single_source}_{i} , where i\in[2,4] , denoting the depth of the corresponding subpage. Similarly, Multi-source QAs are labeled as {multi_source}_{i} , where i\in[2,8] , representing the sum of the depths of the two associated subpages.
claim: WebWalkerQA has single-source (depth 2-4) and multi-source (sum depth 2-8) task types

quote: In this work, we introduce DeepResearch Bench, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating the report generation and web retrieval capabilities of Deep Research Agents.
claim: DeepResearch Bench is the first comprehensive benchmark for Deep Research Agents with 100 tasks across 22 domains

quote: Within the DRA category, Gemini-2.5-Pro Deep Research demonstrates leading overall performance on the RACE framework.
claim: Gemini-2.5-Pro Deep Research achieves top performance with 42.9% accuracy and 111.21 effective citations

quote: RACE(Full) exhibits the strongest overall performance, significantly outperforming both the vanilla baseline and other RACE variants.
claim: RACE evaluation framework shows high consistency with human judgments

quote: We then define the concept of Deep Research tasks as problems requiring agents to conduct multiple rounds of web searches, gather information, perform analysis, and produce high-quality reports.
claim: DeepResearch Bench derived 100 tasks from 96,147 real user queries filtered to 44,019 deep research tasks

quote: Our evaluation methodology focuses on two critical aspects: their capabilities in information retrieval and collection, as well as the quality of the final reports they generate.
claim: DeepResearch Bench uses RACE for report quality evaluation and FACT for citation trustworthiness
